# Preface {.unnumbered}

This report describes an exploratory study of vocabulary development in children with Down syndrome. The study aims to characterise observed trajectories of word learning, spoken and gestured production, and relationships between words understood and produced. Our primary goal is to provide interpretable statistics that can accurately inform expectations, intervention and teaching practice.

To ensure that our findings are broadly representative and to maximise the accuracy of our estimates, we combine multiple data sets from charities and research groups in multiple countries. The combined data include a large number of observations from diverse study populations. We develop statistical models that reflect real world constraints and draw on existing evidence to provide realistic and precise estimates, using an iterative workflow [@gelmanBayesianWorkflow2020; @gelmanStatisticalWorkflow2026]. Developing models also helps us to communicate more clearly -- to be unambiguous about our empirical and statistical assumptions [@farrellComputationalModelingCognition2018]. It also allows us to test and validate these assumptions [@farrellComputationalModelingCognition2018; @mcelreathStatisticalRethinkingBayesian2020]. We fit these models to the data using Bayesian inference [@gelmanBayesianDataAnalysis2013; @wagenmakersBayesianInferencePsychology2018; @mcelreathStatisticalRethinkingBayesian2020; @gelmanRegressionOtherStories2020; @gillBayesianSocialScience2024] to provide intuitive credible intervals.

To contribute to continuing progress, researchers should describe their methods and explain their results in sufficient detail for others to replicate their findings [@korbmacherReplicationCrisisHas2023; @mcelreathReplicationCommunicationPopulation2015].  These descriptions are incomplete without source code that can be run using freely available software [@farrellComputationalModelingCognition2018; @mcelreathStatisticalRethinkingBayesian2020]. This is the goal of this technical report and the accompanying repository ([https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth)).

We have tried to write this report for a broad audience, while aiming to meet recommended reporting practices [@kruschkeBayesianAnalysisReporting2021; @schubertImprovingStatisticalReporting2025]. We cannot avoid statistical and computational details, but we try to explain as much as we can for readers for whom these may not be familiar. For readers who would prefer a more concise and less technical overview of our methods and our findings, a summary report is also available [TODO: link].

To that end, this study is not fixed in time. As new data becomes available, we anticipate updating our estimates and evolving our models. We will version the study as in software development – tagging releases in the study repository whenever we publish updated analyses. We hope that "version 1.0" is helpful and of interest to families, practitioners and researchers alike, and welcome feedback, collaboration, and contributions to future iterations.
